title: MBBS Clinical Year - First Month Foundation
description: A 30-day, 3-hours-per-day introductory tracker across the requested MBBS subjects. This is a first-month foundation plan, not the complete university syllabus.

weeks.title: Week 1 - Clinical foundations
weeks.description: Build a repeatable patient-history and examination method; introduce medicine and surgery fundamentals.
weeks.deliverable: A clinical history/examination checklist and concise medicine/surgery notes.
weeks.objective: Build a repeatable patient-history and examination method; introduce medicine and surgery fundamentals.
reviewChecklist: Daily 3-hour study block completed or honestly rescheduled
Short notes or flashcards created for the week's topics
Clinical examination or case-presentation practice completed where relevant
MCQs or a self-test attempted and mistakes reviewed
Doubts and syllabus-specific details checked against college teaching

days.title: Day 1 - Clinical history taking
days.description: Presenting complaint, chronology, relevant negatives, past/family/personal history, case-sheet structure
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of general medicine for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study the structure of a complete clinical history (45 min)
Write a sample history for fever or abdominal pain (45 min)
Revise vital signs and general examination sequence (45 min)
Create a one-page history-taking checklist (45 min)

days.title: Day 2 - General physical examination
days.description: Pulse, BP, respiratory rate, temperature, SpO2; pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, lymph nodes, oedema
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of general medicine for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study vital-sign measurement and normal adult ranges from college notes (45 min)
Learn the sequence of general physical examination (45 min)
Practise describing pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, nodes and oedema (45 min)
Make an examination checklist and self-test (45 min)

days.title: Day 3 - Cardiovascular examination
days.description: Chest pain, dyspnoea, palpitations, syncope; pulse, JVP, precordium, heart sounds and murmur introduction
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of general medicine for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn focused history for chest pain, dyspnoea, palpitations and syncope (45 min)
Study cardiovascular examination steps and JVP basics (45 min)
Understand S1, S2, added sounds and basic murmur description (45 min)
Practise a short cardiovascular case presentation (45 min)

days.title: Day 4 - Respiratory examination
days.description: Cough, sputum, haemoptysis, breathlessness; inspection, palpation, percussion, auscultation; normal and added sounds
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of general medicine for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study respiratory symptom analysis (45 min)
Learn the respiratory examination sequence (IPPA) (45 min)
Differentiate normal breath sounds, wheeze and crackles (45 min)
Make a comparison table of common respiratory findings (45 min)

days.title: Day 5 - Surgical history and examination
days.description: Pain, swelling, ulcer, lump; surgical case history; examination sequence; consent and asepsis basics
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of general surgery for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn the approach to pain, swelling, lump and ulcer (45 min)
Study examination of a lump: site, size, shape, edge, consistency and mobility (45 min)
Understand consent, privacy, hand hygiene and aseptic principles (45 min)
Write a structured short case presentation for a lump (45 min)

days.title: Day 6 - Wounds and wound healing
days.description: Wound types, phases of healing, factors affecting healing, infection signs, basic instruments and sutures overview
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of general surgery for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study wound classification and phases of wound healing (45 min)
Learn local and systemic factors affecting healing (45 min)
Identify common basic surgical instruments and broad uses (45 min)
Revise wound infection warning signs and create flashcards (45 min)

days.title: Day 7 - Weekly consolidation 1
days.description: Review clinical history, general examination, CVS, respiratory and surgery basics
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of integrated for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Revise Days 1–6 using active recall (45 min)
Practise one medicine case outline and one surgery short case outline (45 min)
Solve 25–30 introductory MCQs from studied topics (45 min)
List weak areas and doubts for faculty (45 min)

weeks.title: Week 2 - Core clinical subjects
weeks.description: Develop first-pass foundations in obstetrics, gynaecology, paediatrics and orthopaedics.
weeks.deliverable: Antenatal, menstrual, paediatric and musculoskeletal quick-reference notes.
weeks.objective: Develop first-pass foundations in obstetrics, gynaecology, paediatrics and orthopaedics.
reviewChecklist: Daily 3-hour study block completed or honestly rescheduled
Short notes or flashcards created for the week's topics
Clinical examination or case-presentation practice completed where relevant
MCQs or a self-test attempted and mistakes reviewed
Doubts and syllabus-specific details checked against college teaching

days.title: Day 8 - Normal pregnancy foundations
days.description: Maternal physiological changes, antenatal booking, gravida/para/abortions/living, EDD concept, antenatal visits
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of obstetrics & gynaecology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study basic obstetric terminology used in class (45 min)
Learn components of an antenatal booking history (45 min)
Understand physiological changes in pregnancy by system (45 min)
Practise EDD calculation using the standard method (45 min)

days.title: Day 9 - Antenatal care
days.description: Antenatal assessment, routine investigations, nutrition, danger signs and high-risk pregnancy concept
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of obstetrics & gynaecology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study the structure of a routine antenatal visit (45 min)
Make a checklist of routine antenatal investigations from college notes (45 min)
Learn pregnancy danger signs and need for urgent assessment (45 min)
Create a one-page antenatal care summary (45 min)

days.title: Day 10 - Menstrual history and common complaints
days.description: Menstrual history, AUB terminology, amenorrhoea, dysmenorrhoea, vaginal discharge; focused history
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of obstetrics & gynaecology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn systematic menstrual and gynaecological history taking (45 min)
Study definitions and broad classification of AUB (45 min)
Review introductory approach to amenorrhoea and dysmenorrhoea (45 min)
Practise a structured history for abnormal uterine bleeding (45 min)

days.title: Day 11 - Paediatric history and growth
days.description: Age-specific history, birth history, immunisation, nutrition, growth charts and developmental milestones
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of paediatrics for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn antenatal, natal and postnatal history components (45 min)
Study feeding, nutrition and immunisation history (45 min)
Understand growth charts and growth monitoring (45 min)
Review developmental domains and make a milestone overview (45 min)

days.title: Day 12 - Newborn foundations
days.description: Newborn history, immediate assessment, APGAR concept, danger signs, thermoregulation and feeding basics
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of paediatrics for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study normal newborn characteristics and immediate assessment (45 min)
Understand APGAR components and limitations (45 min)
Learn newborn danger signs and thermal care/feeding principles (45 min)
Practise a newborn case-history outline (45 min)

days.title: Day 13 - Musculoskeletal history and examination
days.description: Bone/joint pain, swelling, deformity, trauma history; inspection, palpation, ROM and neurovascular assessment
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of orthopaedics for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn focused history for trauma, bone pain and joint pain (45 min)
Study musculoskeletal examination sequence (45 min)
Understand distal neurovascular assessment after limb injury (45 min)
Practise documenting a joint examination (45 min)

days.title: Day 14 - Fracture and trauma basics
days.description: Fracture terminology, open vs closed fractures, displacement, basic X-ray views and initial trauma assessment
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of orthopaedics for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study fracture terminology and common patterns (45 min)
Understand initial trauma assessment and limb-protection principles (45 min)
Learn a basic fracture X-ray checklist: view, alignment, bone, joint, soft tissue (45 min)
Review warning features of compartment syndrome (45 min)

weeks.title: Week 3 - ENT, eye and allied clinical skills
weeks.description: Learn symptom-led assessment and introductory examination across ENT, ophthalmology, skin and psychiatry.
weeks.deliverable: ENT, eye, dermatology and psychiatry symptom/examination summaries.
weeks.objective: Learn symptom-led assessment and introductory examination across ENT, ophthalmology, skin and psychiatry.
reviewChecklist: Daily 3-hour study block completed or honestly rescheduled
Short notes or flashcards created for the week's topics
Clinical examination or case-presentation practice completed where relevant
MCQs or a self-test attempted and mistakes reviewed
Doubts and syllabus-specific details checked against college teaching

days.title: Day 15 - Weekly consolidation 2
days.description: Review OBGYN, paediatrics and orthopaedics foundations
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of integrated for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Revise Days 8–13 using recall questions and diagrams (45 min)
Practise antenatal, paediatric and musculoskeletal case outlines (45 min)
Solve 25–30 MCQs from this week's topics (45 min)
Update weak-topic list and spaced-revision plan (45 min)

days.title: Day 16 - Ear: symptoms and examination
days.description: Ear anatomy overview, otalgia, otorrhoea, hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo, otoscopy, Rinne and Weber
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of ent for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Revise external, middle and inner ear anatomy clinically (45 min)
Learn focused history for ear pain, discharge and hearing loss (45 min)
Understand otoscopy and purpose of Rinne and Weber tests (45 min)
Make a symptom-to-differential table for ear complaints (45 min)

days.title: Day 17 - Nose and throat basics
days.description: Nasal obstruction, epistaxis, rhinorrhoea, sore throat, dysphagia, hoarseness; basic examination
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of ent for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn focused history for nasal obstruction and epistaxis (45 min)
Study common causes and assessment of sore throat and hoarseness (45 min)
Understand basic nose, oral cavity and oropharynx examination (45 min)
Practise a short ENT case presentation (45 min)

days.title: Day 18 - Basic eye examination
days.description: Visual acuity, pupils, ocular movements, external eye examination, torchlight examination and red eye approach
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of ophthalmology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn visual acuity assessment and testing each eye separately (45 min)
Study pupil examination and extraocular movements (45 min)
Understand the introductory approach to red eye and painful eye (45 min)
Practise documenting a basic eye examination (45 min)

days.title: Day 19 - Visual symptoms and fundus basics
days.description: Visual loss, watering, discharge, floaters, flashes; direct ophthalmoscope, slit lamp and normal fundus landmarks
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of ophthalmology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn history taking for visual loss (45 min)
Understand purpose and basic use of direct ophthalmoscopy (45 min)
Study normal fundus landmarks at an introductory level (45 min)
Create a symptom-based ophthalmology revision sheet (45 min)

days.title: Day 20 - Describing skin lesions
days.description: Primary/secondary lesions, morphology, distribution, configuration, colour, scale and structured skin examination
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of dermatology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn primary lesions: macule, papule, plaque, vesicle, bulla, pustule, nodule (45 min)
Study secondary lesions: scale, crust, erosion, ulcer, fissure, scar, lichenification (45 min)
Understand distribution, configuration and morphology (45 min)
Practise describing five example lesions using textbook images (45 min)

days.title: Day 21 - Common dermatology patterns
days.description: Eczema/dermatitis, psoriasis, fungal infection and acne overview; morphology and differential approach
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of dermatology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study introductory features of eczema and psoriasis (45 min)
Review superficial fungal infections and distribution patterns (45 min)
Understand acne morphology and grading concept (45 min)
Build a comparison table using approved clinical images (45 min)

weeks.title: Week 4 - Imaging and perioperative foundations
weeks.description: Build introductory understanding of radiology and anaesthesia, then integrate clinical reasoning.
weeks.deliverable: A modality comparison, chest X-ray checklist and anaesthesia monitoring summary.
weeks.objective: Build introductory understanding of radiology and anaesthesia, then integrate clinical reasoning.
reviewChecklist: Daily 3-hour study block completed or honestly rescheduled
Short notes or flashcards created for the week's topics
Clinical examination or case-presentation practice completed where relevant
MCQs or a self-test attempted and mistakes reviewed
Doubts and syllabus-specific details checked against college teaching

days.title: Day 22 - Psychiatric interview and MSE
days.description: Rapport, psychiatric history, appearance, behaviour, speech, mood, thought, perception, cognition and insight
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of psychiatry for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn rapport building and psychiatric history taking (45 min)
Study components of mental status examination (45 min)
Understand mood vs affect, thought form vs content, insight vs judgement (45 min)
Write a sample MSE from a fictional case (45 min)

days.title: Day 23 - Common psychiatric presentations
days.description: Depression, anxiety, psychosis, substance-use history, suicide-risk enquiry principles and stigma-free communication
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of psychiatry for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study introductory presentations of depression and anxiety (45 min)
Understand psychosis-related symptoms and neutral enquiry (45 min)
Learn substance-use history and non-judgemental communication (45 min)
Review safety-focused suicide-risk enquiry with faculty guidance (45 min)

days.title: Day 24 - Imaging foundations
days.description: X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI; indications, strengths, limitations, radiation safety and image orientation
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of radiology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Compare X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI and their broad uses (45 min)
Learn X-ray orientation, projections and image-quality checks (45 min)
Understand ionising vs non-ionising radiation and safety principles (45 min)
Identify modality and orientation in ten teaching images (45 min)

days.title: Day 25 - Systematic chest X-ray reading
days.description: Chest X-ray approach, normal anatomy, image quality and introductory patterns: consolidation, effusion, pneumothorax
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of radiology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn a systematic chest X-ray reading sequence (45 min)
Practise checking rotation, inspiration, projection and exposure (45 min)
Review common patterns using teaching images (45 min)
Write three structured descriptions of normal or teaching chest X-rays (45 min)

days.title: Day 26 - Pre-anaesthetic assessment
days.description: Focused history, airway assessment overview, fasting principles, ASA physical status concept and consent
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of anaesthesiology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Study goals and components of pre-anaesthetic evaluation (45 min)
Understand airway assessment and basic airway red flags (45 min)
Learn ASA physical status as a risk-description framework (45 min)
Review fasting guidance from current institutional teaching material (45 min)

days.title: Day 27 - Monitoring and recovery basics
days.description: Pulse oximetry, ECG, BP, capnography; general vs regional anaesthesia overview; post-anaesthesia recovery
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of anaesthesiology for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Learn what pulse oximetry, ECG, NIBP and capnography measure (45 min)
Compare general, regional and local anaesthesia at a high level (45 min)
Study goals of post-anaesthesia monitoring and recovery assessment (45 min)
Create a monitoring-device summary and self-test (45 min)

days.title: Day 28 - Integrated clinical reasoning
days.description: Presenting complaint, problem representation, differential diagnosis, investigation rationale, documentation and communication
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of integrated for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Summarise a fictional case in two or three lines (45 min)
Create a short differential diagnosis and justify each possibility (45 min)
Choose suitable introductory investigations and state the clinical question (45 min)
Practise explaining consent, uncertainty and follow-up in patient-friendly language (45 min)

weeks.title: Week 5 - Consolidation and review
weeks.description: Check retention, practise case presentation and MCQs, identify gaps and plan Month 2.
weeks.deliverable: A first-month self-assessment, weak-topic list and Month 2 priorities.
weeks.objective: Check retention, practise case presentation and MCQs, identify gaps and plan Month 2.
reviewChecklist: Daily 3-hour study block completed or honestly rescheduled
Short notes or flashcards created for the week's topics
Clinical examination or case-presentation practice completed where relevant
MCQs or a self-test attempted and mistakes reviewed
Doubts and syllabus-specific details checked against college teaching

days.title: Day 29 - Month-end revision: core subjects
days.description: Consolidate medicine, surgery, obstetrics and gynaecology foundations
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of integrated for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Revise medicine and surgery notes; practise one short case presentation (45 min)
Revise antenatal care, menstrual history and obstetric terminology (45 min)
Solve 30 MCQs from topics studied this month and review explanations (45 min)
Record topics needing faculty clarification (45 min)

days.title: Day 30 - Month-end revision: allied subjects
days.description: Consolidate paediatrics, orthopaedics, ENT, ophthalmology, dermatology, psychiatry, radiology and anaesthesia
objectives: Understand first-month foundations of integrated for this topic
Connect theory with history taking, clinical examination or image interpretation where relevant
Create concise notes and record doubts to clarify with faculty

tasks.title: Revise one-page summaries and image-based notes (45 min)
Practise MSE, skin-lesion description and basic eye/ENT examination outlines (45 min)
Review chest X-ray approach and anaesthesia monitoring concepts (45 min)
Complete a 30-question mixed self-test and analyse mistakes (45 min)
